===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|la:datum<ety:from<la:data>>}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|data}}, nominative plural of {{m|la|datum|t=that is given}}, neuter past participle of {{m|la|dō|t=to give}}; {{surf|en|datum<alt:dat(um)>|-a<id:Latin plural>|nocap=1}}. {{doublet|en|date}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-}}

# {{senseid|en|information, mass sense, especially structured info}} {{lb|en|collective|computing}} A [[representation]] of [[information]] in a [[computer]] (as [[symbol]]s, [[quantity|quantities]], [[sound]], [[image]]s or [[video]]s) which is [[store]]d, [[process]]ed or [[transmit]]ted in the form of electrical [[signal]]s, [[record]]s on [[magnetic tape]] or [[punched card]]s, etc.
#: {{ux|en|'''Data''' can be sent through email.}}
# {{lb|en|collective}} [[material|Material]] recorded and known or assumed as [[fact]]s and used as a basis for [[reasoning]], [[discussion]], or [[calculation]], represented especially in the form of [[number]]s, and usually [[structured]] (such as [[statistics]]).
#: {{nearsyn|en|dataset|data set|data points}}
#: {{ux|en|This '''data''' shows that X is correlated with Y.}}
#* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=vii|text=With fresh material, taxonomic conclusions are leavened by recognition that the material examined reflects the site it occupied; a herbarium packet gives one only a small fraction of the '''data''' desirable for sound conclusions. Herbarium material does not, indeed, allow one to extrapolate safely: what you see is what you get{{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=76
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21579801-making-sense-statistics-riddle-our-days-snakes-and-ladders Snakes and ladders]
|passage=Risk is everywhere.{{...}}For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you. “The Norm Chronicles”{{...}}aims to help '''data'''-phobes find their way through this blizzard of risks.}}
# {{senseid|en|telephony}}{{lb|en|mobile telephony}} {{ellipsis of|en|mobile data|t=digital information transmitted using the cellular telephone network rather than [[Wi-Fi]]}}.
#: {{ux|en|run out of '''data'''}}

====Usage notes====
* The word ''data'' was traditionally seen as [[plural]] of {{m|en|datum}}, but in recent usage, it has been shifting to being a mass noun.<ref>{{quote-web|en|title=Is `data' singular or plural?|work=AskOxford.com|publisher=w:Oxford University Press|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20011101002407/http://www.askoxford.com/asktheexperts/faq/aboutgrammar/data|url=http://www.askoxford.com/asktheexperts/faq/aboutgrammar/data|archivedate=2001-11-01|nodate=1}}</ref><ref>{{R:American Heritage Dictionary}}</ref> Some [[style guide]]s still {{glossary|prescribe}} the count sense, with certain exceptions given (e.g., ''[[big data]]'').
* The definition of {{m|en||data}} in the computing context is from an [http://www.iso.org/iso/catalogue_detail.htm?csnumber=7229 international standard vocabulary] and is meant to distinguish {{m|en||data}} from {{m|en|information}}. However, this distinction is often ignored by the computing profession.<ref>{{quote-journal|en|archivedate=13 January 2026|url=https://figshare.utas.edu.au/articles/journal_contribution/The_Great_Term_Robbery/23204417?file=40900658|title=The Great Term Robbery|author=Neville Holmes|publisher=IEEE Computer
Society|page=96|issn=0018-9162|journal=Computer|date=2001-04-30|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260113082506/https://figshare.utas.edu.au/articles/journal_contribution/The_Great_Term_Robbery/23204417?file=40900658}}</ref>
